lucy: quick Q — I got a 502 in the Console for req id `req_4a7f2c9a`. Where do I grab the raw pod/edge logs for that request?
mike: Console -> Requests page is fastest: paste the req id in the search box, open the request detail, there's a "View raw logs" link that shows correlated lines (if ingestion has them).
lucy: I can't find it on Console, maybe it's sampled out?
jordan: If Console doesn't have it, try the CLI quick hunt:
```
# show request metadata
rb request show req_4a7f2c9a
# stream logs from the service and grep for the req id
stern -n prod "service-myapp" --since 1m | rg "req_4a7f2c9a"
# or use kubectl for specific pod
kubectl logs -n prod pod/myapp-abc123 -c myapp | rg "req_4a7f2c9a"
```
mike: Also note: some proxies rewrite the header. Check both `X-Request-Id` and `x-request-id`, and the edge header `x-rw-request` which we still see on older edge versions.
lucy: how do I map a trace id to logs? I have `trace: 4a6f2b9c`.
jordan: Use the trace lookup then use the span IDs to correlate:
```
rb traces lookup 4a6f2b9c  # gives spans + service names
# then grep logs for span id or the req id found in span attributes
stern -n prod 'service-.*' --since 5m | rg "4a6f2b9c|spanId=...|req_4a7f2c9a"
```
mike: If you rely on OpenTelemetry sampling, some traces won't have full logs — traces are sampled at 1% by default for external traffic. Logs should still exist unless ingestion dropped them.
lucy: I ran stern and nothing. Should I look at ingress/edge logs?
jordan: Yes — edge sits before our pods so if the request failed at the proxy you'll see the req id there. Example: `kubectl -n infra logs -l app=edge-proxy | rg req_4a7f2c9a`
ops-bot: deploy-bot: deployment myapp/2026-03-12-17:02 succeeded :white_check_mark:
mike: If edge logs are missing too, check the log-ingest shard for that time (we had a shard outage on 2026-02-28 that dropped ~12h). Ping me the req id and timestamp and I can check raw ELK ingress retention.
lucy: thanks — timestamp was 2026-03-12T17:01:34Z. Pasting the req id here: `req_4a7f2c9a`.
jordan: OK I'm looking — give me 5.
mike: FYI, small cheat: the Console deep-link `https://console.redwood.ai/requests/req_4a7f2c9a` sometimes returns raw JSON when Console UI fails. Works for quick copy/paste.
jordan: found it in edge logs — looks like the backend timed out after 10s and we returned 502. Lines: `edge=ingress-1 req=req_4a7f2c9a upstream=10.0.12.45:8080 status=504 backend=service-myapp`
lucy: perfect, that's enough to debug. If anyone else hits this and Console search is empty, try the steps above or ping eng-platform. :thumbsup:
